s:

s:
India's Third Moon Mission Chandrayaan-3 made its landing on August 23, 2023.
Which of the following statements is/are correct in this regard.

I. India became the fourth country to land on the moon

II. India became the first country to land on the south pole of the moon.
x:
Most books and keys: Both I and II. Strictly: India landed near the south pole (~69°S, Shiv Shakti Point), not at the pole, and was the 4th to soft-land (impacts by others came earlier) (PMF S&T Part 2 p.15; NextGen S&T Part 2 p.48).
On 23 August 2023 India became the 4th country to soft-land on the Moon (after the USA, USSR and China) and the first to land near its south pole, so both are taken as correct.

Lunar lander will be known as ‘Vikram’ and rover will be known as ‘Pragyan’.
Lunar lander will be known as ‘Vikrant’ and rover will be known as ‘Pragyant’.

x: Chandrayaan-3 kept the Chandrayaan-2 names: the lander is Vikram and the rover Pragyan. Option 1 swaps them; Vikrant is the aircraft carrier.

x: The rover's APXS (Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer) derives the elemental composition (Mg, Al, Si, K, Ca, Ti, Fe) of soil and rocks at the site; ILSA records moonquakes and LRA is NASA's laser retroreflector.

s:

s:

x:

x: Moon Express got US FAA approval on 3 August 2016 – the first private mission plan to go beyond Earth orbit to the Moon.

x: NASA's SOFIA (an airborne infrared observatory) confirmed water on the Moon's sunlit surface in October 2020. Orion is a crew capsule; Gemini and Mercury were 1960s crewed programmes.

x: The Soviet Luna 2 was the first spacecraft to reach the Moon's surface (impact, September 1959). Ranger 4 (1962) was the first US impact, Surveyor 4 failed, and Chang'e-1 (2007) was an orbiter; the first soft landing was Luna 9 (1966).

s: Weightlessness is –
x:

The mass of the object will increase
